blog_summary: Adrian Colyer reviews Chapter 3 of Dr. Howard’s PhD thesis, which systematizes major revisions to the classic Paxos consensus algorithm. The post highlights several optimizations and refinements to Paxos, including the use of negative acknowledgements (NACKs) to eliminate timeout delays, bypassing phase two when a value is already decided, and introducing an optional phase three to improve termination. Other notable optimizations include the distinguished proposer (leader) optimization to avoid proposer duels, phase ordering to reduce round trips, and Multi-Paxos for consensus over sequences of values. The post also discusses roles, epoch management, and proposal copying as further refinements to improve efficiency and robustness.
